title: Prompts, Tokens, and Context Windows
description: Learn how prompts are structured, how tokens affect cost and behavior, and how context windows limit RAG and agent design.

blocks.text: A prompt is the complete input sent to an LLM: system instructions, retrieved context, tool descriptions, and the user message. Tokenization splits that input into chunks the model can process. Every prompt is bounded by a context window, which limits how much information you can include in a single request.

When you add retrieved documents to a prompt, you consume tokens. If retrieval returns ten long passages, you may exceed the context window or leave too few tokens for the model to generate a useful answer. In .NET backends, this means you must control chunk count, chunk size, and reranking quality.

blocks.title: Common backend mistake
blocks.text: Returning too much retrieved context is worse than returning slightly less highly relevant context. Prefer reranking and truncation over naive top-k retrieval.

blocks.title: Prompt composition with token-aware design
blocks.content: Compose a system prompt, retrieved context, and user message safely using Microsoft.Extensions.AI.

blocks.title: Typical prompt sections
items: **System prompt** — sets persona, rules, safety, and output format.
**Tool schema** — describes available functions for models that support tool calling.
**Retrieved context** — inserted documents or summaries relevant to the user request.
**Conversation history** — prior user and assistant turns.

items.text: I can explain why token count affects both cost and quality
items.hint: Longer prompts cost more and reduce room for generation; truncated context degrades answers

items.text: I can list the common sections of a production prompt
items.hint: System prompt, tool schema, retrieved context, conversation history, user message

items.text: I understand why context windows constrain RAG design
items.hint: More chunks consume tokens and may crowd out useful generation space

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Prompts combine system instructions, tools, retrieved context, and user input.
Tokens are the unit of billing and reasoning capacity.
Context windows limit how much retrieval you can safely include.
blocks.takeaway: Backend AI is partly a token budgeting problem. Design retrieval and prompt composition around the model's context limits.
